stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether the color of a drink affects the ability to identify its flavor. They recruited 70 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition tasted ten fruit drinks whose colors did not match their flavors. Participants in the other condition tasted the same ten drinks with matching colors. The researchers then recorded the number of flavors out of ten that each participant named correctly.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether keeping a gratitude journal raises well-being. They recruited 110 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition wrote down three things they were grateful for every night for a month. Participants in the other condition wrote down three things they had done every night for a month. The researchers then recorded each participant's rating of life satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 10 at the end of the month.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group on the waiting list

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 300 fifth-grade students. For each one, they recorded working memory span and reading comprehension score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.52.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

Researchers investigated whether children imitate aggressive behavior that they observe. They recruited 72 preschool children and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition watched a video of an adult hitting an inflatable doll. Children in the other condition watched a video of an adult playing quietly with other toys. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child hit the doll during ten minutes of free play.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They hypothesized that the study method would affect memory for a passage.

**Participants.** The sample was 120 university students, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

**Results.** The group that took practice quizzes: mean score on the final test (%) = 68. The group that reread the passage: mean score on the final test (%) = 49. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does sleep improve memory?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 60 students learned a list of word pairs at 9 p.m. Half were randomly assigned to sleep normally and half to stay awake all night. Twelve hours later, the sleep group recalled a mean of 31 pairs out of 40 and the awake group recalled a mean of 22 (p = 0.01).

**Source B.** Researchers recorded the brain activity of 25 adults in a sleep laboratory after they had learned a maze. The more slow-wave (NREM stage 3) sleep a participant had, the faster that participant completed the maze the next morning (r = +0.55).

**Source C.** A survey of 900 high school students found that those who reported sleeping fewer than six hours on school nights had lower average grades than those who slept eight hours or more. The researchers noted that students who slept less also reported more stress and more hours of paid work.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes generativity versus stagnation?

options.text: Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are
options.why: That describes identity versus role confusion.

options.text: Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret
options.why: That describes integrity versus despair.

options.text: Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships
options.why: That describes intimacy versus isolation.

options.text: Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work
options.why: Correct. This is what generativity versus stagnation means.

questions.explanation: Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels?

options.why: An elicitor is an event or stimulus that triggers an emotion.
The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
Correct. Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.

questions.explanation: Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.
Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: Which part of a neuron contains the nucleus?

options.why: The axon terminals is the endings of the axon that release neurotransmitters.
Correct. The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.
The axon is the long fiber that carries the neural impulse away from the cell body toward other cells.
The synapse is the tiny gap between the sending neuron and the receiving neuron.

questions.explanation: The cell body is the part of the neuron that contains the nucleus and keeps the cell alive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The number of stressful life events in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.
Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

options.text: The number of colds in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: A two-year-old insists, 'Me do it!' when getting dressed. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Correct. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.

questions.explanation: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.stem: A child uses one mental category, 'chair', for stools, armchairs and benches. This mental category is an example of which of the following?

options.why: Accommodation is the changing of an existing schema to fit new information.
A prototype is the best or most typical example of a category.
A schema is a mental framework that organizes and interprets information.
Correct. A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.explanation: A concept is a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.why: This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

options.text: The number of other people present
options.why: This is the independent variable.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.

options.text: The time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: The group with mismatched colors named fewer flavors correctly. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: The color of the drinks caused the difference in flavor identification
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The color of the drinks and flavor identification are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = +0.50. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship with the negative sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: Around age 51, Mrs. Ortiz's menstrual cycles stop permanently. Which term describes this change?

options.why: Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Correct. Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Puberty is the period of sexual maturation, when a person becomes able to reproduce.
Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.

questions.explanation: Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.

questions.stem: Scores on the odd-numbered questions of a test closely match scores on the even-numbered questions. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Correct. Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.explanation: Split-half reliability is the consistency of scores between two halves of the same test.

questions.stem: Ben always plans ahead, meets every deadline and keeps his desk tidy. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Correct. Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.
Emotional stability is the Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.explanation: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.stem: After watching her older brother tie his shoes, four-year-old Lily ties her own in the same way. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.
Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
Correct. Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.

questions.explanation: Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.

questions.stem: A dog's salivation to a tone has died away. The next day, the tone is sounded and the dog salivates again. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.
Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.
Correct. Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.explanation: Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of a weakened conditioned response after a rest period.

questions.stem: A sleeper's EEG shows large, slow delta waves, and she is very difficult to wake. Which stage of sleep is she in?

options.why: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
Correct. NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.
The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.explanation: NREM stage 3 is the deep sleep stage marked by slow delta waves, in which a person is hard to wake.

questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the assistants who recorded the results knew which condition each participant was in. What is this procedure called?

options.why: Random sampling is how participants are chosen from a population.
That is a therapy technique, not a research control.
In a single-blind procedure only the participants are unaware.
Correct. Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.explanation: Keeping both participants and researchers unaware of the conditions reduces bias from expectations.

questions.stem: Signals from the eyes, ears and skin pass through one structure that routes them to the correct areas of the cortex. Which structure is this?

options.why: The medulla is the base of the brainstem, which controls heartbeat and breathing.
The cerebellum is the structure at the back of the brainstem that coordinates balance, movement and procedural learning.
Correct. The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.
The reticular activating system is the network of neurons in the brainstem that controls arousal and alertness.

questions.explanation: The thalamus is the brain's sensory relay station, which directs incoming signals to the cortex.

questions.stem: Rubbing a bumped elbow reduces the pain because the touch signals close off the pain signals in the spinal cord. Which theory explains this?

options.why: Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Correct. The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.explanation: The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm?

options.why: Temperament is a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity, which appears early in life.
Authoritarian parenting is the parenting style that sets strict rules and expects obedience, with little warmth or discussion.
Correct. Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.
Permissive parenting is the parenting style that makes few demands and sets few limits.

questions.explanation: Authoritative parenting is the parenting style that sets firm rules but explains them, listens and is warm.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes depolarization?

options.text: The level of stimulation that must be reached for a neuron to fire
options.why: That describes the threshold.

options.text: The process in which the sending neuron reabsorbs leftover neurotransmitters from the synapse
options.why: That describes reuptake.

options.text: The rule that a neuron either fires at full strength or does not fire at all
options.why: That describes the all-or-nothing principle.

options.text: The change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative
options.why: Correct. This is what depolarization means.

questions.explanation: Depolarization is the change in which positive ions rush into the axon and make the inside less negative.

questions.stem: After two neurons fire together repeatedly, the synapse between them becomes more efficient. What is this process called?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Correct. Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes constructive memory?

options.text: The building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information
options.why: Correct. This is what constructive memory means.

options.text: The inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned
options.why: That describes source amnesia.

options.text: The increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it
options.why: That describes imagination inflation.

options.text: The distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event
options.why: That describes the misinformation effect.

questions.explanation: Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care?

options.why: A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
Cultural humility is a therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view.
Correct. Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.

questions.explanation: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.stem: A doctor prescribes a drug that blocks dopamine receptors to reduce a patient's hallucinations. Which kind of drug is this?

options.why: Correct. An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.
An antianxiety drug is a drug that reduces tension by depressing central nervous system activity and can be addictive.
An antidepressant is a drug, such as an SSRI, that treats depression and anxiety by raising the availability of serotonin or norepinephrine.
Lithium is the mood-stabilizing drug used to treat bipolar disorder.

questions.explanation: An antipsychotic drug is a drug that reduces hallucinations and delusions by blocking dopamine receptors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better?

options.why: Downward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing worse.
An external locus of control is the belief that outcomes are decided by luck, fate or other people.
Correct. Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.
An internal locus of control is the belief that a person controls their own outcomes through their own actions.

questions.explanation: Upward social comparison is the comparing of oneself with people who are doing better.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses?

options.why: Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Correct. The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.explanation: The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes restoration?

options.text: The theory that dreaming helps sort and strengthen the day's memories
options.why: That describes the consolidation theory.

options.text: The theory that dreams are the brain's attempt to make sense of random neural activity during sleep
options.why: That describes the activation-synthesis theory.

options.text: The repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep
options.why: Correct. This is what restoration means.

options.text: The strengthening of memories that takes place during sleep
options.why: That describes memory consolidation.

questions.explanation: Restoration is the repair of body and brain tissue that takes place during sleep.

questions.stem: A dentist's drill causes pain, and soon the sound of the drill alone makes Ben tense. In this example, the sound of the drill is which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.
The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.explanation: The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options?

options.why: An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.
Intrinsic motivation is the desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying.
Correct. An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.explanation: An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Consent is obtained before the study.
Replication is repeating a study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity?

options.why: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Social loafing is the tendency for people to put in less effort when working in a group than when working alone.
Correct. Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.explanation: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior?

options.why: A defense mechanism is in psychodynamic theory, a method the ego uses without awareness to reduce anxiety by distorting reality.
Correct. The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.
A projective test is a personality test, such as an inkblot test, that asks people to interpret unclear images in order to reveal hidden feelings.
Unconditional positive regard is the attitude of total acceptance toward another person, whatever they say or do.

questions.explanation: The unconscious is in psychodynamic theory, the store of thoughts, wishes and memories that a person is not aware of but that still influences behavior.

questions.stem: Antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Correct. Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain?

options.why: Correct. Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.
Ataque de nervios is the culture-bound anxiety syndrome, found mainly among people of Caribbean descent, marked by shouting, crying and a feeling of being out of control.
A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.explanation: Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.

questions.stem: A therapist and client rank situations from 'looking at a picture of a spider' to 'holding a spider.' What is this ranked list called?

options.why: A token economy is the behavioral system in which people earn tokens for desired behavior and exchange them for rewards.
Aversion therapy is the behavioral treatment that pairs an unwanted behavior with an unpleasant stimulus.
Applied behavior analysis is the use of the principles of conditioning to increase helpful behaviors and reduce harmful ones.
Correct. A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.

questions.explanation: A fear hierarchy is a list of feared situations arranged from the least to the most frightening.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The gratitude group was also phoned each week by a friendly researcher
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: The two groups differed in subjective well-being at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the type of journal
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes mental age?

options.text: The theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal
options.why: That describes multiple intelligences.

options.text: The level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test
options.why: Correct. This is what mental age means.

options.text: The steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations
options.why: That describes the Flynn effect.

options.text: Originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100
options.why: That describes the intelligence quotient.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: If the data were shown on a scatterplot, what pattern would the points form?

options.text: A loose band that slopes upward from left to right
options.why: Correct. A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

options.text: A shapeless cloud with no slope
options.why: That would show a correlation near zero.
Only a correlation of +1.00 or −1.00 gives a perfect line.

options.text: A loose band that slopes downward from left to right
options.why: That would show a negative correlation.

questions.explanation: A moderate positive correlation appears as a band of points sloping upward.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: A four-year-old enjoys pretend play and talks well, but thinks a tall glass holds more juice than a wide glass with the same amount. Which of Piaget's stages is he in?

options.why: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.
Correct. The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.explanation: The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.

questions.stem: A three-year-old says 'I runned fast' and 'two foots'. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Cooing is the vowel-like sounds, such as 'ooh', that infants make from about two months.
Telegraphic speech is the two-word stage in which a child uses mostly nouns and verbs, such as 'want juice'.
The one-word stage is the stage from about age 1 in which a child speaks mostly in single words.
Correct. Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.explanation: Overgeneralization is the applying of a grammar rule too widely, as in 'goed' or 'mouses'.

questions.stem: A patient stands rigid in one position for several hours and does not respond to anyone. Which symptom is this?

options.why: Correct. Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.
A hallucination is a sensory experience, such as hearing voices, that occurs without any outside stimulus.
A delusion is a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that a person holds despite clear evidence against it.
Disorganized speech is the jumbled, illogical speech, sometimes called word salad, that is a symptom of schizophrenia.

questions.explanation: Catatonia is a disturbance of movement in which a person may remain motionless for hours or move without purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension?

options.why: Correct. Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.
Contralateral control is the arrangement in which each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body.
Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.

questions.explanation: Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.stem: A therapist uses relaxation training with one client, examines thinking patterns with another and combines both with a third. Which approach is this?

options.why: The biopsychosocial model is the view that disorders result from the interaction of biological, psychological and social factors.
The diathesis-stress model is the view that a disorder develops when an inherited vulnerability is triggered by stressful experience.
Correct. An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.
Comorbidity is the presence of two or more disorders in the same person at the same time.

questions.explanation: An eclectic approach is the use of techniques from several types of therapy, depending on the client's problem.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also test hypotheses.
Experiments also use numerical data.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus?

options.why: Correct. Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.

questions.explanation: Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.

questions.stem: Kim remembers exactly where she sat and what she ate at her tenth birthday party. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Correct. Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.
Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.explanation: Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the participants to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which term refers to a language's complete system of rules, including both semantics and syntax?

options.why: Semantics is the rules by which we get meaning from words and sentences.
A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.
Correct. Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.explanation: Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends?

options.why: Correct. Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.
Deception is the misleading of participants about the true purpose of a study, allowed only when necessary and followed by debriefing.
Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.

questions.explanation: Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman?

options.why: Correct. Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.
Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.
Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.

questions.explanation: Gender is the socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the tendency to remember the first items in a list well?

options.why: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.
Correct. The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.

questions.explanation: The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is an in-depth study of one individual.
That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Someone checks their phone repeatedly for a message that could arrive at any time. Which schedule of reinforcement is this?

options.why: A variable-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after an unpredictable number of responses.
A fixed-ratio schedule is the schedule in which the behavior is reinforced after a set number of responses.
Correct. A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.
A fixed-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after a set amount of time is reinforced.

questions.explanation: A variable-interval schedule is the schedule in which the first response after an unpredictable amount of time is reinforced.

questions.stem: A scientist explains color vision by saying that the retina's cones come in three kinds, each most sensitive to one color. Which theory is this?

options.why: Monochromatism is a rare form of color blindness in which a person sees only shades of gray.
Prosopagnosia is the inability to recognize faces, even familiar ones, after brain damage.
Correct. The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.explanation: The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input?

options.why: Correct. A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: A tumor just above the ear disrupts a patient's ability to process sounds. Which lobes are affected?

options.why: The occipital lobes is the lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information.
Correct. The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.
The frontal lobes is the lobes behind the forehead, which handle planning, judgment and voluntary movement.
The parietal lobes is the lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information.

questions.explanation: The temporal lobes is the lobes above the ears, which process sound and help recognize language.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes ethnocentrism?

options.text: An unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members
options.why: That describes prejudice.

options.text: The tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture
options.why: Correct. This is what ethnocentrism means.

options.text: Unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members
options.why: That describes discrimination.

options.text: The tendency to believe that people get what they deserve
options.why: That describes the just-world phenomenon.

questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.

questions.stem: Rex looks for excitement through wild parties and reckless, uninhibited behavior. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Correct. Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.explanation: Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.stem: A depressed client believes she is worthless, that the world is unfair and that nothing will ever improve. This pattern is called which of the following?

options.why: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Correct. The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.
Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.explanation: The cognitive triad is the pattern of negative thoughts about oneself, the world and the future that is found in depression.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.52, +0.12, +0.05, +0.35. Which coefficient shows the strongest relationship?

options.why: +0.12 is closer to zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; −0.52 is farthest from zero.
+0.05 is closer to zero.
+0.35 is closer to zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. −0.52 is farthest from zero.

questions.stem: A stranger risks her life to pull a child out of a river and expects nothing in return. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The social reciprocity norm is the expectation that people will help those who have helped them.
Burnout is the physical and emotional exhaustion that results from long-term stress at work.
The social responsibility norm is the expectation that people will help those who need help, even at a cost to themselves.
Correct. Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.explanation: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of others.

questions.stem: Before the study could begin, a committee at the university reviewed the plan to make sure the children would be protected from harm. What is this committee called?

options.why: A confederate is someone who secretly works for the researcher.
That is a discussion group used to collect opinions.
Correct. An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.
That is a comparison condition.

questions.explanation: An institutional review board must approve research with human participants.

questions.stem: Inside the spinal cord, some cells link the incoming pain message to the outgoing movement message. Which cells are these?

options.why: Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Correct. Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.

questions.explanation: Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.stem: To treat severe epilepsy, surgeons cut the fibers that carry messages between the left and right hemispheres. Which structure was cut?

options.why: The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.
The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
Correct. The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The cerebral cortex is the wrinkled outer layer of the brain, which handles thinking, perception and voluntary movement.

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.

questions.stem: Newly hatched ducklings follow the first moving thing they see, a researcher, as if he were their mother. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: A teratogen is a harmful agent, such as alcohol or a virus, that can damage an embryo or fetus.
The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.
Correct. Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
Fine motor skills is the movements that use small muscles, such as grasping a crayon or buttoning a shirt.

questions.explanation: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes maintenance rehearsal?

options.text: The rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail
options.why: That describes highly superior autobiographical memory.

options.text: The memory of the events of one's own life
options.why: That describes autobiographical memory.

options.text: The linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory
options.why: That describes elaborative rehearsal.

options.text: The repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory
options.why: Correct. This is what maintenance rehearsal means.

questions.explanation: Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sublimation?

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: That describes regression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: Correct. This is what sublimation means.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Mr. Hale's house is so full of old newspapers and boxes that he cannot reach his bed, yet he cannot bear to discard anything. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Posttraumatic stress disorder is the disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event.
Correct. Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.
A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.
Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten?

options.why: Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Correct. Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.
Long-term memory is the relatively permanent and limitless store of knowledge, skills and experiences.

questions.explanation: Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.

questions.stem: Which research method did the researchers use?

options.why: No variable was manipulated and there was no random assignment.
A case study examines one individual in depth.
A meta-analysis combines the results of many studies.
Correct. The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.explanation: The researchers measured two variables and examined their relationship without manipulating anything.

questions.stem: A driver cuts in front of Ruth, and she immediately concludes he is a rude person, never considering that he may be rushing to a hospital. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.
An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
The self-serving bias is the tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors.
Correct. The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.explanation: The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others?

options.why: Dependent personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an excessive need to be taken care of and by clinging, submissive behavior.
Correct. Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.
Narcissistic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by an exaggerated sense of self-importance and a need for admiration.
Histrionic personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by excessive emotion and attention seeking.

questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is the personality disorder marked by a lack of conscience and disregard for the rights of others.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 15. About what percentage of scores are between 55 and 85?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: About 68% of scores fall within one standard deviation of the mean. (55 and 85 are one standard deviation from the mean; 40 and 100 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of memory for a passage

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of memory for a passage.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Memory for a passage was defined as the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that took practice quizzes scored higher. On average, the value was 68 for the group that took practice quizzes and 49 for the group that reread the passage, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 120 university students from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that took practice quizzes scored higher. (68 compared with 49).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the study method affects memory for a passage. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the study method. The finding illustrates the testing effect: retrieving information strengthens memory more than rereading it.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does sleep improve memory?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Sleep improves memory because memories are consolidated during sleep.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, students who slept recalled a mean of 31 of 40 word pairs, compared with 22 for students who stayed awake.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through memory consolidation: during sleep, the hippocampus and cortex strengthen newly encoded memories, so the sleep group stored the word pairs better. Because the study was an experiment with random assignment, sleep can be said to have caused the difference.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants who had more slow-wave sleep completed the maze faster the next morning (r = +0.55).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because NREM stage 3 sleep is linked to strengthening the neural connections formed during learning (long-term potentiation), so more deep sleep goes with better retention of the maze.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
